name: Wikidata
what: Open structured knowledge base; humans are items with instance-of Q5 and carry IDs for most other people databases.
why_it_matters: Backbone identifier hub for the people graph; most other rows here map to a Wikidata property.
numbers: Direct instance-of human: 6,376,879 items (2025 workshop page); with subclasses about 10.3M (older query page, 2018). Run the Q5 count yourself for a live figure.
ui_notes: Query service at query.wikidata.org (SPARQL); Special:Statistics for totals.
note: Counts disagree by method; the two sources are dated. | check: Wikidata SPARQL today: ?p wdt:P31 wd:Q5 returns 13,738,279 (row 6,376,879 is a stale 2025 figure, about half the live count).

name: Pantheon 1.0 (MIT Media Lab)
what: Manually verified dataset of globally famous biographies with birth data, gender, occupation taxonomy and popularity scores, built from Wikipedia language editions.
why_it_matters: Closest existing notability ranking for people; its popularity score and occupation taxonomy are reusable ranking signals.
numbers: 11,341 biographies appearing in 25+ Wikipedia languages (Scientific Data, PMC4700860).
ui_notes: Downloadable data and an online explorer; check for a newer Pantheon release before use.
note: Search returned only Pantheon 1.0 material; newer versions unconfirmed. Popularity is Wikipedia-based, which critics say is not universal fame. | check: PMC4700860 abstract: Pantheon 1.0 includes 11,341 biographies present in more than 25 Wikipedia languages; matches row.

name: Human Biographical Record (HBR), Nekoei and Sinn
what: Notable-people dataset with Wikidata as backbone and Wikipedia text from all 292 language editions.
why_it_matters: Large, multilingual notable-people base with text; a direct comparator for a people graph.
numbers: More than 7 million notable individuals (CEPR DP15825).
note: Access terms not checked.

name: Cross-verified Database of Notable People 3500BC-2018AD (Laouenan et al.)
what: Notable-people database built from Wikipedia and Wikidata editions with each field cross-checked across sources.
why_it_matters: Cross-verification method is the quality bar for merging person records.
numbers: More than 2 million individuals (search summary of Scientific Data 2022 paper).
note: The 2 million figure came from a search summary; confirm in the paper.

name: Notable people database (Gergaud et al., HAL)
what: Notable people extracted from Wikipedia biographies, with associated locations.
why_it_matters: Provides person-to-place links, which the people graph needs for geography.
numbers: 1,243,776 notable people and 7,184,575 associated locations (HAL record).
note: Titled A Brief History of Human Time.

name: Wiki people (Douwe Osinga)
what: Browsable database of people built from Wikidata, limited to humans with English Wikipedia articles, born 1500-2010.
why_it_matters: Working example of a people browser built on Wikidata that can be copied for UI ideas.
numbers: About 1.9 million people (project page, via search summary).
note: Hobby project; freshness unknown.

name: wikidata-bulk-people (PyPI)
what: Python tool that extracts structured person records from Wikipedia and Wikidata at scale to JSONL, CSV or SQL.
why_it_matters: Ready-made extractor for loading the people graph from dumps.
numbers: No counts given on the package page.
note: Read the source before running any package code.

name: FamilySearch Prominent Persons Index (Wikipedia)
what: US-focused index of notable people from Wikipedia with name, birth and death dates and places, and a link to the Wikipedia page.
why_it_matters: Genealogy-side notability index with date and place fields for matching.
numbers: Coverage 1500-2022 (collection page); record count not captured.
note: Login needed; not checked.

name: Wikiquote
what: Open quotation wiki with one page per person, licensed CC BY-SA, covering many languages.
why_it_matters: Main open source of attributed quotes per person, keyed to Wikidata.
numbers: About 168,000 articles in 89 languages as of 10 May 2014 (Meta-Wiki); current total not found.
note: Count is from 2014; check the live statistics page.

name: Quote Garden API
what: Free REST API of famous quotes with author names.
why_it_matters: Cheap quote source to test attribution pipelines.
numbers: More than 5,000 quotes (publicapis.io listing).
note: License not checked; the listing links to the service rather than the provider.

name: They Said So Quotes API
what: Hosted quotes API with lookup by author, category or tag.
why_it_matters: Commercial quote-by-author source if Wikiquote coverage is thin.
numbers: Pricing not captured.
note: Commercial; check terms before use.

name: Iconic Quotes API (Zyla Labs)
what: Marketplace quotes API with a free trial and paid tiers.
why_it_matters: Another quote feed to compare for coverage and price.
numbers: Free trial of 3 test requests; Pro plan lists 10,000 calls (listing).
note: Listing copy reads like marketing; quote sources unverified.

name: IMDb Non-Commercial Datasets (name.basics)
what: Daily TSV dumps of IMDb titles and people, including name.basics with person ID, name, birth and death years, professions and known-for titles.
why_it_matters: Largest free film and TV people index with stable IDs (nconst) for linking.
numbers: Full set about 1 GB (pimdb docs); row counts for name.basics not captured.
note: Personal and non-commercial use only; the download host is datasets.imdbws.com.

name: Open Library (authors)
what: Internet Archive book catalog with author records, monthly bulk dumps and a JSON API.
why_it_matters: Open author records with IDs that link to Wikidata and VIAF.
numbers: About 6 million authors and over 20 million editions (site, via search summary).
note: Author endpoint paths not confirmed.

name: MusicBrainz
what: Open music metadata database with artist records typed as Person, Group and so on, plus full PostgreSQL dumps.
why_it_matters: Open artist IDs (MBIDs) with person typing, useful for musicians in the people graph.
numbers: 2,872,200 artists (May 2026 mirror statistics); about 53.7% typed Person (mirror page).
note: Figures are from third-party mirrors; confirm on musicbrainz.org. | check: musicbrainz.org/statistics (updated 2026-10-13): 3,012,034 artists (row 2,872,200, -4.7%, within 10%); Person 53.6% (row 53.7%).

name: ORCID
what: Registry of researcher identifiers with a free public API and an annual CC0 public data file.
why_it_matters: Authoritative researcher identity layer for authors and scientists.
numbers: Passed 10 million iDs in late 2020; annual public data file (2023 edition, CC0) (ORCID pages).
note: Live total not found; check the ORCID statistics page.

name: OpenAlex
what: Open index of works, authors, institutions and topics with a free REST API and full dumps.
why_it_matters: Largest open author-disambiguated index for scholars; useful for research people.
numbers: 2022 paper: 209M works and 2013M disambiguated authors (figure as reported; likely a typo, check); later counts higher (arXiv 2205.01833).
note: Author disambiguation is the weakest area per the paper. | check: api.openalex.org today: 326,886,422 works and 96,474,526 authors; row's '2013M authors' is implausible (about 20x live) and the 209M works figure is out of date.

name: Discogs
what: Music marketplace and database with artist, label and release pages, plus monthly data dumps.
why_it_matters: Large crowd-built artist index, strong for electronic and vinyl artists.
numbers: Passed 5 million artists in 2017 and 10 million releases in 2018 (press milestones); dump sizes not captured.
note: Milestone figures are dated; check the data dumps page.

name: Find a Grave
what: User-built memorial database of burial sites and people, with bios and family links.
why_it_matters: Large dated-death index for people, and Wikidata P1036 links to it.
numbers: 13.7M memorials added in 2023 (site's own year review); about 180M entries in FamilySearch index (2019 blog).
note: Copyright and terms apply; the OSM wiki advises Wikidata over ref:find_a_grave.

name: Prabook
what: Free English biographical encyclopedia founded in 2018, with profile pages for professionals.
why_it_matters: Large professional-bio source for business and academic people.
numbers: Profile count not found.
note: Operator named as The World Biographic Encyclopedia, Inc. Check for terms before scraping.

name: Oxford Dictionary of National Biography
what: Authoritative UK biography reference with peer-reviewed lives and full-text search.
why_it_matters: High-quality bios for British and Commonwealth people, a quality benchmark for descriptions.
numbers: Over 60,000 lives (library pages); 54,922 lives in 50,113 articles in the 2005 print edition (ABR review).
ui_notes: Free to UK library members via library login.
note: Not open access; licensed.

name: Deutsche Biographie (NDB, ADB)
what: Online German biography database covering the NDB and ADB, with a name index of persons and families.
why_it_matters: Authoritative German-language biographies and an index with cross-links.
numbers: About 50,000 full biographies (ADB, NDB, NDB-online); claims 1,000,000+ personalities and families indexed (homepage via search); NDB print 27 volumes, 23,000+ people (Wikipedia).
note: The 1M figure and 50k figure differ in scope; the gap is not explained.

name: Notable Names Database (NNDB)
what: Biographical database with executive summaries, career timelines, and a visual connection mapper.
why_it_matters: Adds connection data between people, which is an edge type for the graph.
numbers: Over 40,000 people (search summary of Wikipedia-derived text).
note: Status disputed: some sources say no updates since 2022.

name: Behind the Name
what: Given-name etymology database run since 1996 by one owner, covering names from many cultures and fiction.
why_it_matters: Name-to-meaning and gender metadata for name parsing in person records.
numbers: 30,549 names in the main database and 219,570 in the submitted database (About page).
note: Names, not people; included for name-parsing use.

name: The Movie Database (TMDB)
what: Film and TV database with person endpoints for cast and crew, birthdays, places of birth and images.
why_it_matters: Film and TV people with images and cast links, a strong complement to IMDb IDs.
numbers: Free non-commercial API with attribution; free tier rate limit 40 requests per 10 seconds (third-party summary).
ui_notes: Requires API key (v3) or read token (v4).
note: Commercial use needs a separate agreement per the third-party summary; confirm on TMDB terms.

name: The Interviews: An Oral History of Television (Television Academy Foundation)
what: Video oral-history archive of television pioneers, with full interviews online.
why_it_matters: Long-form first-person interviews with dated career detail, good for quote and biography extraction.
numbers: 900 interviews, about 3,700 hours (2018 finding aid, OAC); over 950 pioneers (Wikipedia); over 3,000 hours (2022 NEH note).
note: Counts differ by date; roughly 900 to 950 interviews.

name: Computer History Museum oral histories
what: Transcribed oral histories and panels with computing pioneers, with audio, video and transcript PDFs as separate records.
why_it_matters: Dense career-history transcripts for tech people; good for linking people to projects.
numbers: Over 1,000 interviews and panels; catalog holds 151,130+ records (search summary).
ui_notes: Each interview has an audio or video record and a transcript record.
note: Exact interview count not confirmed.

name: WikiTree
what: Free collaborative family-tree wiki with one profile per person and sourced biographies.
why_it_matters: Large connected family graph with sources; good for kinship edges.
numbers: 25 million profiles (2020, EOGN); more than 36 million profiles claimed late 2023 (via Wikipedia mirror).
note: Profile quality varies; wiki-style collaboration.

name: Congress.gov API and Biographical Directory (bioguide)
what: Official member API from the Library of Congress with bioguide IDs, plus ProPublica's Congress API mirror of member data.
why_it_matters: Public-domain legislator IDs (bioguide) for US politicians.
numbers: Covers all members since 1789 per the congress-legislators dataset (GitHub).
note: Community dataset found; the canonical unitedstates/congress-legislators repo was not checked. Official api.congress.gov docs not opened.

name: OpenSanctions PEP Core Data
what: Consolidated politically exposed persons dataset from hundreds of government sources, with people, positions and relationships.
why_it_matters: Officials and their positions with IDs, useful for political-role edges.
numbers: 2,030,394 total entities; about 757,000 people; about 225,000 positions (dataset page, processed 2025-08-30).
note: Business use needs a paid license per the summary. | check: opensanctions.org/datasets/peps live: 1,973,054 total entities (row 2,030,394, -2.8%), 726,408 people (row 757k, -4%), 211,392 positions (row 225k, -6%); all within 10%, row is a 2025-08-30 snapshot.

name: OpenSanctions Wikidata PEPs
what: Politically exposed persons derived from Wikidata, updated daily.
why_it_matters: Wikidata-based PEP subset that is easy to map to Q-IDs.
numbers: 183,139 entities (OpenSanctions PEP overview page).
note: Derived from Wikidata.

name: Miller Center Presidential Oral History Program
what: Oral histories with leaders of US presidential administrations since 1981, some embargoed.
why_it_matters: Primary first-person accounts of federal officials, dated and attributable.
numbers: Clinton project 134 interviews; Obama transcripts for cleared interviews released March 2026 (Duke hub and HNN summaries).
note: Some interviews are restricted; the total was not captured.

name: Pushshift Reddit dataset
what: Archive of Reddit submissions and comments with a researcher API and monthly dumps.
why_it_matters: Account-level posting history for public people with Reddit accounts.
numbers: 651M submissions and 5.6B comments for 2005-2019 (ICWSM 2020 paper).
ui_notes: Researcher API runs queries over the full archive.
note: Current availability after the 2023 API changes not confirmed; treat as possibly restricted and check before use.

name: Forbes Real-Time Billionaires (via third-party scrapers)
what: Forbes's live billionaire ranking, exposed by community scrapers; no official Forbes API found.
why_it_matters: Wealth-based ranking of people with industry and country fields.
numbers: 3,400+ profiles per live list; scraper priced from $1.00 per 1,000 profiles (Apify listing); Kaggle snapshot 2,657 rows.
note: Scraping may breach Forbes terms; check first. | check: Apify listing: pricing from $1.00 per 1,000 billionaire profiles (matches); the 3,400+ live-list count was not checked.

name: Wikimedia Pageviews API (top articles)
what: Public, keyless API of daily per-article views, with a top-1000 endpoint per project and per country.
why_it_matters: Attention signal for ranking people by public interest, the basis of notability-rank proxies.
numbers: Top 1,000 per project per day (Compute Edge listing); Pew used it for monthly person rankings 2015-2025.
note: Confirm endpoints on the Wikimedia REST docs.

name: Internet Archive TV News Archive
what: Recorded US TV news with closed-caption search, so public figures' spoken words can be found and clipped.
why_it_matters: Transcript-level search of what public figures said on TV, with timestamps.
numbers: Recording since 2009 (Syracuse guide); Trump Archive held 700+ speeches and interviews (2017 news item).
note: Features described from older sources; verify on archive.org.

name: Tapesearch
what: Podcast transcript search with timestamps, free basic tier and paid Pro.
why_it_matters: Searchable spoken words from podcast guests, a quote source for people.
numbers: 878,000+ transcripts from 4,670+ podcasts (third-party listing).
note: Coverage figures from a listing site; check Tapesearch directly.

name: Audioscrape
what: Podcast transcript search across millions of hours with speaker filters.
why_it_matters: Speaker-filtered search across podcasts, directly useful for who-said-what.
numbers: Millions of hours (vendor docs, via search summary); pricing not captured.
note: Vendor product; check terms.

name: Particle Podcast Intelligence
what: API-style podcast index with diarized, speaker-identified transcripts.
why_it_matters: Speaker-identified podcast data for developers, a feed for quote attribution.
numbers: 100,000+ shows indexed (search summary).
note: Vendor page; the Particle site itself was not opened.

name: Bluesky academic dataset (Pisa/CNR, Zenodo v3)
what: Full post histories and follow, repost, quote and comment graphs for Bluesky users.
why_it_matters: Account-level social graph and posting history for public people on Bluesky.
numbers: Over 4 million users (81% of registered accounts), 235M posts (Zenodo v3, Jan 2025).
note: v1 and v2 are restricted; use v3. Contains personal data, so IRB and privacy review needed.

name: OSoMe social media archives (Indiana University)
what: Bluesky firehose and Mastodon post archives for research.
why_it_matters: Continuous stream of public social posts for account-level studies.
numbers: Bluesky firehose from Aug 2023, updated daily; Mastodon from more than 50 instances (OSoMe page).
note: Academic-affiliate access only; not anonymized. | check: osome.iu.edu/resources/data-resources-bak returns HTTP 404; the cited OSoMe data page is not at this URL (row's claim unsupported by its source).

name: Getty ULAN (Union List of Artist Names)
what: Controlled vocabulary of artists, with biographies, roles and nationality, released as linked open data.
why_it_matters: Artist identity and role vocabulary with stable IDs for art people.
numbers: 525,315 person or corporate records, 1,483,920 names (Getty FAQ, Aug 2024).
note: ODC BY 1.0 license; not comprehensive.

name: VIAF (Virtual International Authority File)
what: OCLC-run cluster of authority records for persons, organisations and works, linked across national libraries.
why_it_matters: Cross-national identity clusters for author and person disambiguation.
numbers: 37 agencies in 29 countries (OCLC VIAF page); 20M+ clusters (2013 NISO webinar, dated).
note: Open data under ODC-BY per OCLC; current person count not found.

name: ISNI (International Standard Name Identifier)
what: ISO standard identifier for public identities, including creators and people, linked to VIAF.
why_it_matters: Standard identifier for people in libraries and publishing.
numbers: No count found in search.
note: Gap: no ISNI-specific figures; check isni.org.

name: Common Crawl
what: Open web crawl archive in WARC, WAT and WET formats, monthly snapshots.
why_it_matters: Raw source for mining bios, pages and mentions of people at scale.
numbers: Over 8 PiB corpus (Aug 2024 newsletter); CC-MAIN-2026-30 had 2.14B pages (Bright Data summary).
note: Page-count claims partly from a secondary source.

name: Web of Stories
what: Video life stories of scientists, authors, filmmakers and artists, with segments and transcripts.
why_it_matters: Long first-person life-story video for notable scientists and creators.
numbers: Over a hundred short segments per interview (search summary); total count not captured.
ui_notes: Interviews split into segments; YouTube playlists.
note: Notables include Crick, Watson, Wheeler, Sacks, Lessing, Roth. | check: webofstories.com returns 200; site exists. The per-interview segment count was not checked.

name: British Library Voices of Science
what: Oral History of British Science interviews with UK scientists and engineers, with highlights and biographies.
why_it_matters: UK scientist interviews with biographies, a citable source for British science figures.
numbers: Over 100 UK scientists and engineers (BSHS archive note).
ui_notes: Full interviews on British Library Sounds.
note: Launch-era coverage.

name: ParlSpeech (Harvard Dataverse)
what: Full-text parliamentary speeches tagged with speaker, party and date across national lower chambers.
why_it_matters: Attributed speech by named legislators, a direct quote-by-person source.
numbers: 3.9M speeches, 7 countries (original, 2017); V2 6.3M speeches, 9 chambers (Dataverse summary).
note: Dataverse landing page not opened; check DOI and license there.

name: Database of Parliamentary Speeches in Ireland 1919-2013
what: Speech-level database of Dáil debates with TD names and party data.
why_it_matters: Long-run speaker-attributed speech for Irish legislators.
numbers: About 4.5 million speeches from 1,178 TDs (search summary of arXiv 1708.04557).
note: DOI from the paper summary.

name: ParlScot (Scottish Parliament spoken contributions)
what: Dataset of spoken contributions in the Scottish Parliament with party, gender, constituency and region.
why_it_matters: Speaker-attributed contributions with demographic fields for MSPs.
numbers: 1.8 million contributions, 1999-2021 (Strathclyde record).

name: EveryPolitician
what: Open Popolo-format lists of legislators across parliaments, as CSV and JSON.
why_it_matters: Consistent legislator roster across countries with a common schema.
numbers: 100 parliaments at launch (mySociety 2015).
note: Maintenance status unconfirmed.

name: Popit (Sinar Project)
what: Open-source politician and organisation database with Popolo-compliant API.
why_it_matters: Self-hostable Popolo store for politician records, a model for the graph's politician layer.
numbers: Used for Malaysia and Myanmar legislators (Sinar and OpenHluttaw).
note: Code on GitHub at Sinar/popit_ng per summary.

name: Comparative Legislators Database (legislatoR R package)
what: Cross-national legislator database with political, career, sociodemographic, online presence and visual attributes, pulled via Wikidata.
why_it_matters: Ready-made legislator attributes including public attention, useful for ranking politicians.
numbers: Over 67,000 politicians from 16 countries (package manual summary).

name: UK Parliament Members and Committees APIs
what: Official APIs for members, votes, bills, questions and committee activity.
why_it_matters: Official UK member IDs and voting records for politicians.
numbers: Not captured.
note: Open Parliament API directory; developer.parliament.uk cited in summary.

name: Crunchbase (people records)
what: Company and investor database with founder, employee and board data on company and person pages.
why_it_matters: Founder and executive career links for business people.
numbers: Pro $49/mo annual or $99 monthly; Business from $199/mo; API enterprise-only (third-party summaries, 2026).
note: Scraping terms unverified; API access gated.

name: Fundable
what: Startup and investor data API with people records, funding rounds and investor data.
why_it_matters: Self-serve people records for founders and investors as a cheaper alternative to Crunchbase.
numbers: 366k people records, updated daily; 200 requests per minute (vendor claim via listing).
note: Vendor claim; not verified. | check: tryfundable.ai: 366k+ company people (row 366k matches); page says updated multiple times per day, row says daily (minor).

name: ROR (Research Organization Registry)
what: Open registry of research organisations with IDs, operated by Crossref, DataCite and CDL.
why_it_matters: Affiliation identifiers that link people to institutions in the graph.
numbers: Not captured.
note: Institutions, not people; included as the affiliation link layer. CC0, free API and dump.

name: Biography Reference Bank (EBSCO)
what: Licensed biographical database for libraries covering notable people across eras.
why_it_matters: Library-licensed biographies, a source to compare coverage against.
numbers: 996,000 biographical records (search summary citing EBSCO page).
note: Licensed, not open. | check: about.ebsco.com BRB page: 996,000 biographical records (matches row).

name: Letterboxd (film and member data)
what: Film community site with film pages listing directors and cast, plus public member profiles.
why_it_matters: Film crew and cast links with user taste data.
numbers: No official people count; scrapers expose film metadata.
note: Gap: no official open people index found.

name: Rotten Tomatoes community dataset
what: Community project with ratings and reviews plus director and cast fields for films.
why_it_matters: Film cast-to-review links from a community source.
numbers: Over 15,000 movies (project page).
note: Weak source; licence and provenance unknown.

name: Last.fm dataset (Zenodo, 2010)
what: Last.fm user and listening dataset with artists mapped to MusicBrainz IDs.
why_it_matters: Music-artist listening signals keyed to MBIDs.
numbers: About 359,000 users and 186,642 artists with MBIDs (record).
note: Dated; current Last.fm catalog not captured.

name: Wikipedia biographies CSV (Kaggle mirror)
what: CSV of Wikipedia biography infobox, first paragraph and full article text.
why_it_matters: Ready text for bio extraction and person summaries.
numbers: Row count not captured.
note: Mirror of a Hugging Face set; check licence.

name: AGE dataset (IEEE DataPort)
what: Structured dataset of life, work and death records for people, per its title.
why_it_matters: Possible large people set with life-events fields.
numbers: Title states 122 million records; not verified.
note: Only the title was seen; contents and licence not checked. | check: IEEE DataPort page title: 'Age dataset ... of 1.22 million distinguished people'; row says 122 million records (factor of 100 wrong).
